title: Normalized inflation on resolutions and change of the auxiliary group
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] on the small coherent profinite site [def-weil-size-convention]. For a profinite group $P$, write $\mathcal A_P(A)$ for internal $A$-modules with condensed $P$-action [def-sfb-condensed-action-module], and $\Gamma_P$ for sections fixed after every profinite base change. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories and K-injective total right derived functors [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Let $G,L$ be profinite groups, let $K\triangleleft G$ be open normal, and put $Q=G/K$. Write $T(M)=M^K$, with residual $Q\times L$-action, $U$ for forgetting this residual action, and $r=\operatorname{Res}_K$ for action restriction along $k\mapsto(k,1)$. All invariant inclusions and inflation adjunctions have the normalized transposes of [def-sfb-normal-invariant-comparison-data]: restrict codomain to invariants, with inverse given by composing the inclusion. Use the quotient adjunction, K-injective preservation and $\beta:D(U)RT\simeq R\Gamma_KD(r)$ of [lem-sfb-open-normal-action-injective-models], normalized by the identity on $U(TI)=(rI)^K$. The conjugate of the identity between composite exact trivial inflation and trivial inflation to $G\times L$ gives a natural isomorphism
$$c:R\Gamma_{G\times L}\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_{Q\times L}RT.$$
Its component on any K-injective $I$ is the identity $I^{G\times L}=(TI)^{Q\times L}$, and its derived adjunction has exactly the composite unit and counit.

For a module $N$, the canonical unit $\eta_N:T(N)[0]\to RT(N[0])$ is represented on a resolution $i:N[0]\to I$ by $T(i)$. Under $\beta$ its underlying map is $(ri)^K$, the usual map to derived $K$-invariants. If $a:T(N)[0]\to J$ is a K-injective resolution, there is a unique homotopy class $b:J\to TI$ with $ba\simeq T(i)$. The transpose of $b$ under quotient inflation is its composite with the inclusion $TI\hookrightarrow I$; its map on full invariant complexes is $\Gamma_{Q\times L}(b):J^{Q\times L}\to I^{G\times L}$. This map represents the derived inflation attached to the original inclusion $\operatorname{Inf}T(N)\hookrightarrow N$, is independent of all resolutions and lifts, and satisfies
$$c_N\operatorname{inf}_N=R\Gamma_{Q\times L}(\eta_N).$$
These descriptions and the displayed equation are natural in equivariant module maps, while $\beta,c$ are natural on the entire unbounded derived category. For every continuous homomorphism $h:L'\to L$, let $r_h$ denote restriction in the source and quotient action categories, and use primes for the functors with $L'$ in place of $L$. The identity $T'r_h=r_hT$ and the inclusions of full invariants induce derived transformations $b^G_h:R\Gamma_{G\times L}\to R\Gamma_{G\times L'}D(r_h)$ and $b^Q_h:R\Gamma_{Q\times L}\to R\Gamma_{Q\times L'}D(r_h)$, which are the derived restriction transformations $b_u$ of [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus] for $u=1_G\times h$ and $u=1_Q\times h$, together with $\tau_h:D(r_h)RT\to RT'D(r_h)$ derived from that identity. Their square for $c$ is
$$c'_{D(r_h)N}\,b^G_{h,N}=R\Gamma_{Q\times L'}(\tau_{h,N})\,b^Q_{h,RTN}\,c_N.$$
The corresponding square for $\beta$ identifies $D(U')\tau_h$ with the identity of $R\Gamma_KD(r)$, since restriction to $K$ is unchanged. The unit and inflation equation commute with these transformations. More precisely, for K-injective $I$ and any K-injective resolution $a:r_hI\to J$, all the comparisons are the invariant maps induced by $T'(a):T'(r_hI)\to T'J$, with the unchanged $K$-invariants for $\beta$. No preservation of K-injectives by $r_h$ is assumed.

proof.text:
Use [lem-sfb-open-normal-action-injective-models] for the normalized adjunction $\operatorname{Inf}\dashv T$, the full-invariant identities, and K-injective preservation. If $I$ is K-injective, both $TI$ and $\Gamma_{Q\times L}(TI)$ are K-injective. For an arbitrary complex $X$ of quotient-action modules, [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] gives the two outside bijections in
$$\operatorname{Hom}_D(D(\operatorname{Inf})X,I)=\operatorname{Hom}_K(\operatorname{Inf}X,I)=\operatorname{Hom}_K(X,TI)=\operatorname{Hom}_D(X,TI).$$
The middle bijection is termwise normalized adjunction, which takes chain homotopies to chain homotopies. Thus the derived quotient adjunction on these models has the termwise counit inclusion. The identical argument for trivial inflation and full invariants gives their normalized derived adjunctions. Every object admits such a model, so these Hom bijections specify the adjunctions on all of the unbounded categories.

source.place: Agent argument: normalized derived adjunctions from Stacks 070I (lemma-K-injective) and the given exact-inflation adjunctions

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-derived-composition-adjunction-normalization] with $L_a$ exact trivial inflation from $\mathcal A_1(A)$ to $\mathcal A_{Q\times L}(A)$, $L_b$ exact quotient inflation, $L_c$ trivial inflation to $G\times L$, and $\lambda$ the identity $L_bL_a=L_c$; these categories are Grothendieck abelian and the right adjoints $\Gamma_{Q\times L},T,\Gamma_{G\times L}$ are the specified ones by [lem-sfb-open-normal-action-injective-models]. The derived adjunctions it uses are the ones of step 1: at a K-injective target both have the termwise counit class. The underived conjugate $\kappa$ of the identity under the composite adjunction [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] and conjugation [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] is computed by transposes: a map into $I$ goes first to its $K$-fixed codomain, then to its full fixed codomain, and the composite is restriction directly to $I^{G\times L}$. The specified inclusions identify this with $(TI)^{Q\times L}$ by the models lemma, so $\kappa$ is the identity $\Gamma_{G\times L}=\Gamma_{Q\times L}T$. The cited theorem gives $c=\kappa^D$, the conjugate of $D(\lambda)=\mathrm{id}$, whose component on a K-injective $I$ is the class of $C(\kappa)_I$, i.e. the identity of $I^{G\times L}=(TI)^{Q\times L}$ ($TI$ is K-injective), and whose adjunction has exactly the composite unit $R\Gamma_{Q\times L}(\eta^{\operatorname{Inf}})\eta^{\mathrm{triv}}$ and counit $\varepsilon^{\operatorname{Inf}}\operatorname{Inf}(\varepsilon^{\mathrm{triv}})$. Naturality of $c$ on all derived morphisms is part of that statement.

Write $\alpha$ for the computation unit of [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. For a resolution $i:N[0]\to I$, its naturality gives $RT(Qi)\alpha_{N[0]}=\alpha_I Q(Ti)$. Both $RT(Qi)$ and $\alpha_I$ are isomorphisms, so under the canonical identification $RT(N[0])=TI$ the unit is represented by $T(i)$. By [lem-sfb-open-normal-action-injective-models], $\beta_N$ is the identity $UTI=(rI)^K$. Applying $U$ to $T(i)$ therefore gives $(ri)^K$, with its original augmentation. The same computation-unit calculation for $\Gamma_K$ identifies this with the usual map to derived $K$-invariants, as a derived morphism rather than only on cohomology.

Let $a:T(N)[0]\to J$ be the indicated resolution. By [lem-sfb-open-normal-action-injective-models], $TI$ is K-injective. The bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] identifies homotopy classes into $TI$ with derived maps. Since $a$ is a quasi-isomorphism, there is exactly one class $b:J\to TI$ with $[b][a]=[T(i)]$, namely $[T(i)][a]^{-1}$. The normalized quotient adjunction transposes $b$ to $\widetilde b=\iota_I\operatorname{Inf}(b):\operatorname{Inf}J\to I$. It satisfies $\widetilde b\operatorname{Inf}(a)\simeq i\iota_N$, by naturality of the invariant inclusion $\iota$. Exact quotient inflation makes $\operatorname{Inf}(a)$ a quasi-isomorphism. Thus this chain map represents exactly the original inclusion $\operatorname{Inf}T(N)\to N$ under the resolution identifications.

source.place: Agent argument: lift uniqueness and normalized transpose; Stacks 070I (lemma-K-injective)

proof.text: Apply full invariants to the transpose of step 4. By [lem-sfb-open-normal-action-injective-models], its source invariant complex is $J^{Q\times L}$ and its target is $I^{G\times L}=(TI)^{Q\times L}$, and the induced chain map is exactly $\Gamma_{Q\times L}(b)$. This is derived inflation attached to the inclusion: quotient restriction uses the invariant inclusion, as specified by [lem-sfb-condensed-restriction-mate-normalization], and step 4 supplies its coefficient morphism on resolutions. Since $TI$ is K-injective, $R\Gamma_{Q\times L}(\eta_N)$ is represented by the same map $\Gamma_{Q\times L}(b)$. Step 2 identifies $c_N$ with the identity on the target model, giving $c_N\operatorname{inf}_N=R\Gamma_{Q\times L}(\eta_N)$.

source.place: Agent argument: inflation map and equation on actual invariant complexes

proof.text: For an equivariant module map $f:N\to N'$, choose a map $v:I\to I'$ lifting it and $w:J\to J'$ lifting $T(f)$. Such classes exist uniquely by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. Both $T(v)b$ and $b'w$ become $T(i'f)$ after precomposition with $a$; because $TI'$ is K-injective they are homotopic. Applying the additive invariant functor preserves this homotopy, so step 5 is natural in $f$. Repeating with $f$ the identity and different resolutions proves independence of resolutions and lifts; comparison quasi-isomorphisms between K-injectives are homotopy equivalences by the same cited node. The construction of $\beta$ is already natural on the whole derived category by [lem-sfb-open-normal-action-injective-models]; that of $c$ is natural by step 2.

source.place: Agent argument: independence and module-map naturality via unique homotopy classes

proof.text: Fix $h:L'\to L$, a K-injective $I$, and a K-injective resolution $a:r_hI\to J$ in the primed source category. Exactness of $r_h$ follows from [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus]. Define $\tau_{h,QI}$ by $T'(a):r_hTI=T'r_hI\to T'J$, using the computation-unit identifications of [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. Define $b_h^G$ by $\Gamma_{G\times L}I\to\Gamma_{G\times L'}r_hI\to\Gamma_{G\times L'}J$. For $b_h^Q$ start with $TI$, choose a resolution $r_hTI\to V$ with $V$ K-injective, and factor $T'(a)$ through $V$ in the homotopy category. This factorization exists uniquely because $T'J$ is K-injective by [lem-sfb-open-normal-action-injective-models] and [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. Thus the composite $R\Gamma_{Q\times L'}(\tau_h)b_h^Q$ is represented by the invariant inclusion followed by $\Gamma_{Q\times L'}T'(a)$. The normalization identity in [lem-sfb-condensed-restriction-mate-normalization] identifies the two $b$ transformations with the specified derived restriction maps. For a derived morphism between objects represented by K-injectives, [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] represents it by a unique homotopy class. Lifting its restriction to the chosen primed resolutions makes the two composites equal after precomposition with the resolution map; the same Hom bijection makes them homotopic. Thus these constructions are natural on all unbounded derived objects, independently of the chosen resolutions.

source.place: Agent argument: construct auxiliary-group transformations without K-injective preservation by restriction

proof.text: Both sides of the asserted $c$ square are now maps from $I^{G\times L}$ to $(T'J)^{Q\times L'}=J^{G\times L'}$. Step 2 makes the two $c$ components identities; step 7 makes both composites the inclusion of invariant sections followed by the invariant map of $a$. They are therefore equal as chain maps under the displayed identities. The normalizations of [lem-sfb-open-normal-action-injective-models] make the $\beta$ square the map $(rI)^K\to(r'J)^K$ induced by $a$, where $r'r_hI=rI$. Both $rI$ and $r'J$ are K-injective; their comparison is a quasi-isomorphism, hence a homotopy equivalence by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. Under their resolution identifications it represents the identity of $R\Gamma_KD(r)$. This is the claimed identity for $D(U')\tau_h$, not a claim that its chosen chain representative is literally an identity.

source.place: Agent argument: compute both comparison squares on the same fresh resolution

proof.text: For a module resolution $i:N[0]\to I$ use $a r_h(i):r_hN[0]\to J$ as primed resolution. The two unit composites are both $T'(a)r_h(T(i))=T'(a r_h(i))$. On full invariants the corresponding two inclusion composites agree because for every generalized section $x$ fixed by $G\times L$ its image is $a(x)$, fixed by $G\times L'$. Consequently the unit squares commute. Apply the $c$ square of step 8, the two equations of step 5 and the naturality of $b^Q_h$ in derived morphisms ([lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus], applied to $D(r_h)\eta_N$), then cancel the isomorphism $c'$: the inflation square commutes as well. The underlying $K$-invariant unit squares agree by the same calculation and step 8. All calculations allow arbitrary $h$ and use the fresh $J$, so no K-injective preservation by $r_h$ has entered.
